Date. June 19 , 36

Subject Coal Merchants' Association-- meeting.

Made by D.F.S. Lockwood Forwarded by [Signature]

Two hundred members of the Coal Merchants'
Association held a meeting at 2 p.m. June 16 in the office
of the Association, Foh Yeu Road, City, which was presided
over by Mo Chun-fu (毛春圃). Representatives from the
local Tangpu and Chinese Chamber of Commerce attended. The
following resolutions were discussed and passed :-
1. That Tsang Yien-cheng (張延章), proprietor of the Yeu
Sing (又新) Coal Hong, 567 North Szechuen Road, be
expelled from the Association for having filed a suit
against the Association's committee members.
2. That the Tung Dah Zung (敦大成) Hong, 210-4 Chihli Road be
re-admitted as a member of the Association.

With reference to resolution 1, it will be recalled
that the Yeu Sing (又新) Coal Hong was on December 21, 1935,
publicly accused by Feu Yi San (潘以三), a member of the
Coal Merchants' Association, of dealing in Hopei Coal. Feu
Yi San stated that the Yeu Sing Coal Hong had disobeyed
instructions issued by the Coal Merchants' Association,
which prohibited members of the association in dealing in
coal mined from the Liu Kieng Coal Mine. This mine was
seized by the Japanese during the latter part of 1935.
Resolution 2 refers to the Tung Dah Zung Co. which
was expelled from the association in December, 1935, for
dealing in Hopei coal.

日期：1936年6月19日

主题：煤业公会——会议。

呈报人：D.F.S. Lockwood 转呈人：[签名]

6月16日下午2时，煤业公会二百名会员在位于华界福州路的公会办公室举行会议，由毛春圃（Mo Chun-fu）主持。当地塘浦代表及华人商会代表出席了会议。讨论并通过了以下决议：
1. 又新（Yeu Sing）煤号业主、北四川路567号的张延章（Tsang Yien-cheng），因对公会委员提起诉讼，被开除出公会。
2. 敦大成（Tung Dah Zung）煤号（直隶路210-4号）重新获准成为公会会员。

关于决议1，需回顾的是，1935年12月21日，煤业公会会员潘以三（Feu Yi San）公开指控又新（Yeu Sing）煤号经营河北煤。潘以三称，又新煤号违抗了煤业公会发布的指令，该指令禁止会员经营柳江煤矿开采的煤炭。该矿于1935年下半年被日本人占领。
决议2涉及敦大成公司，该公司曾于1935年12月因经营河北煤而被开除出公会。

Threatening letters received by Coal Merchants in the
Settlement from the BranchOffice of Blood Soul Corps
(血魂团上海分团).

A.C.P. Uyehara received information from the Japanese
Consulate through the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha, 185 Szechuen Road
to the effect that threatening letters from the Anti-Japanese
Party had been received by various coal merchants who are
dealing in Woo Po coal through the above mentioned Japanese firm
and consequently instructions were received to make enquiries.

The undersigned proceeded to the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha
No.185 Szechuen Road where Mr. S. Ohta, sub-manager in the
Coal Department of the above firm was interviewed and the
following facts ascertained.

During November 1935, the above mentioned firm imported
a quantity of Woo Po coal (乌煤) from Northern China
approximately 8,000 tons, and established an individual Chinese
coal dealer named Chong Foo Coal Co. (忠孚煤号) at No.805
Dixwell Road for specially dealing in Woo Po coal in Shanghai.

Previous to the establishment of the above stated coal
firm, the Shanghai Coal Merchants Association held a meeting and
subsequently decided to boycott the above coal when it arrived
in Shanghai. The first boat load arrived on the 28/11/35 and
coal in question was sold in Shanghai cheaper than any other coal,
consequently a number of merchants opened transaction through
Chong Foo Coal Co.

As the previous decision of the Coal Merchants' Association
was not steadfastly observed by the merchants for dealing with
Woo Po coal, eventually the Association split into two parties.
The opposition party had removed Association to Chapei while the
other remained in the teashop at No.462 Chekiang Road.

Since both parties began opposing each other, the coal
merchants dealing in Woo Po coal have been treated and obstructed
by the other party, and the following information were furnished:-
(1) Sing Nyi Koon Coal Shop (信义公煤号), No.149/20
Changsha Road was bombed on the 6/1/36.
(2) Manager of the In Yuen Coal Shop (永元煤号) in
Chapei suffered injury by Sulphuric acid in Chapei
on 20/1/36.
(3) The undersigned Coal shops in the Settlement received
threatening letters from Branch office of Blood
Soul Corps (血魂团上海分团).
The translation and a copy of photograph of same
are attached to this report.
Yoong Lee Coal Shop (永利煤号), 7 Dixwell Road
Chong Foo Coal Shop (忠孚), 805 Dixwell Road.
Yuen Yih Zung Coal Shop (元一成), 6 lane 169 Fearon Road.
Dung Foo Zung Coal Shop (敦福成), 210-214 Chihli Road.
Yah Loong Coal Shop (亚隆), 356 Range Road.
Yung Moo Coal Shop (永茂), 28 Wenshow Road.
Jih Sung Zung Coal Shop (日成), 1302 Penang Road.

As to the above Mr. Ohta requested the S.M.P. to take
necessary measures to protect those merchants from further
incidents. Small meeting of the merchants dealing in Woo Po
coal (30 to 40 in number) have been taking place in the La Ta
Keh (拉达阁) teashop at No.462 Chekiang Road from 1 p.m.
to 3 p.m. daily. The first meeting after Chinese New Year'
holiday will be held on the 28/1/36.

关于租界内煤商收到来自血魂团上海分团的恐吓信

上原（Uyehara，音译）助理警务处长通过四川路185号的三井物产株式会社从日本领事馆获悉，通过各种日本商行从事乌煤交易的多家煤商收到了来自反日党派的恐吓信，因此接到指令进行调查。

本人前往四川路185号的三井物产株式会社，会见了该公司煤炭部副经理大田 S. 先生（S. Ohta，音译），并查明了以下事实。

1935年11月期间，上述公司从中国北方进口了约8,000吨乌煤，并在狄思威路805号设立了一家名为“忠孚煤号”的中国个体煤商，专门在上海经销乌煤。

在上述煤号成立之前，上海煤业公会曾召开会议，随后决定抵制这批煤炭运抵上海。第一批货轮于1935年11月28日抵达，涉案煤炭在上海的售价比其他任何煤炭都便宜，因此许多商人通过忠孚煤号开展交易。

由于商人们并未坚定遵守煤业公会此前关于抵制乌煤的决定，最终公会分裂为两派。反对派已将公会迁至闸北，而另一派则留在浙江路462号的茶楼内。

自从两派开始相互对立以来，从事乌煤交易的煤商一直受到另一派的对待和阻挠，并提供如下信息：
(1) 长沙路149/20号的“信义公”煤号于1936年1月6日被炸。
(2) 闸北“永元”煤号的经理于1936年1月20日在闸北遭受硫酸伤害。
(3) 租界内的下列煤号收到了来自血魂团上海分团的恐吓信。
译文及照片副本附于本报告之后。
永利煤号，狄思威路7号
忠孚煤号，狄思威路805号
元一成煤号，斐伦路169弄6号
敦福成煤号，直隶路210-214号
亚隆煤号，兰路356号
永茂煤号，文秀路28号
日成煤号，槟榔路1302号

关于上述情况，大田先生请求上海公共租界工部局警务处采取必要措施，保护这些商人免受进一步事件侵害。从事乌煤交易的商人小型集会（人数约30至40人）每日下午1时至3时在浙江路462号的拉达阁茶楼举行。春节假期后的第一次集会将于1936年1月28日举行。

members of the Coal Merchants' Association on January 12,

January 7, 1936.

Bomb explosion at the Singh Nyi Kung Coal Company

At 2.05 p.m. January 6, an unidentified male Chinese deposited a wooden bucket containing a bomb of the canister type inside the main entrance of the Sing Nyi Kung Coal Company ( 信 义 公 ), No.20, Lane 149, Changsha Road. An explosion ensued and a number of windows of the premises were shattered. Among the debris was found a letter in Chinese purporting to emanate from the "Shanghai Branch of t e Flood & Soul Group" and addressed to two share-holders of the coal company. The letter accuse the addresses of conspiring with traitors and threatens further action should the warning be ignored.

This act of intimidation is believed to be the outcome of a dispute over the sale locally of coal mined in the province of Hopei.

At 2.5 p.m. January 6, 1936, a bomb explosion occurred
inside the front entrance of a Chinese type of dwelling house,
at No.20, Lane 149, Changsha Road. This house is situated in
an alleyway midway between Changsha and Wenchow Roads and
part of it is utilized as an office by the Sing Nyi Kung Coal
Company. The remainder is occupied by one of the shareholders
of the company named Loo Teh-yeu(羅德佑).

Access to the outer compound of the house was gained
through an unlocked swing door. Further access was barred
by an iron grille which was locked. The bomb, which was of the
tin canister type, had been carried to the scene in a wooden
bucket. The explosion of the bomb blew the bucket to pieces
and a number of windows of a partition dividing the inner and
outer compounds were broken. The partition was also slightly
damaged. No one was injured. Pieces of the bucket found
show that it had been used to contain paint or plaster; small
pieces of a brush, such as used by painters, were also found.
The bucket had also contained a letter. This letter is
decipherable although damaged by the explosion, and purports to
emanate from the "Shanghai Branch of the Blood and Soul Corps"
and contains threats of further action against traitors.
(Translation attached).

According to an apprentice of the coal company, named
Sz Tsih-hwa(史濟華), a man dressed in blue clothing (Chung
San style), height about 5'5", medium build, deposited the
bomb, but his face was not seen.

This act of intimidation appears to centre round a
dispute over the sale of "Hopei" coal in Shanghai. Agitation
has been in progress locally for some time over the ownership

1936年1月6日下午2时05分，长沙路149弄20号一处中式住宅的前门内发生炸弹爆炸。该房屋位于长沙路与温州路之间的一条弄堂中段，部分被信义公煤号用作办公室。其余部分由该公司一位名为罗德佑（Loo Teh-yeu）的股东居住。

通过一扇未上锁的弹簧门进入该房屋的外院。进一步进入被一道上锁的铁栅栏门阻挡。炸弹为锡罐式，装在一个木桶内带至现场。炸弹爆炸将木桶炸成碎片，分隔内外院的隔墙上的多扇窗户玻璃破碎。隔墙也受到轻微损坏。无人受伤。发现的木桶碎片显示其曾用于盛放油漆或灰泥；还发现了画家所用刷子的小碎片。桶内还有一封信。尽管信件因爆炸受损，但仍可 decipherable（译出），声称发自“血魂团上海分团”，包含对汉奸采取进一步行动的威胁。（附译文）。

据该煤号一名名为史济华（Sz Tsih-hwa）的学徒称，一名身穿蓝色服装（中山装样式）、身高约5英尺5英寸、中等身材的男子放置了炸弹，但未看清其面部。

此次恐吓行为似乎围绕在上海销售“河北”煤炭的纠纷展开。当地关于所有权

January 7, 1935.
Bomb Explosion at the Sing Nyi Kung Coal Company,
House No.2, Lane 149, Changsha Road.

At 2.5 p.m. January 6, 1936, a bomb explosion occurred
inside the front entrance of a Chinese type of dwelling house,
at No.20, Lane 149, Changsha Road. This house is situated in
an alleyway midway between Changsha and Wenchow Roads and
part of it is utilized as an office by the Sing Nyi Kung Coal
Company. The remainder is occupied by one of the shareholders
of the company named Loo Teh-yeu (羅德佑).

Access to the outer compound of the house was gained
through an unlocked swing door. Further access was barred
by an iron grille which was locked. The bomb, which was of the
tin canister type, had been carried t. the scene in a wooden
bucket. The explosion of the bomb blew the bucket to pieces
and a number of windows of a partition dividing the inner and
outer compounds were broken. The partition was also slightly
damaged. No one was injured. Pieces of the bucket found
show that it has been used to contain paint or plaster; small
pieces of a brush, such as used by painters, were also found.
The bucket had also contained a letter. This letter is
decipherable although damaged by the explosion, and purports to
emanate from the "Shanghai Branch of the Blood and Soul Corps"
and contains threats of further action against traitors.
(Translation attached).

According to an apprentice of the coal company, named
Sz Tsih-hwa (史濟華), a man dressed in blue clothing (Chang
San style), height about 5' 5", medium build, deposited the
bomb, but his face was not seen.

This act of intimidation appears to centre round a
dispute over the sale of "Hopei" coal in Shanghai. Agitation
has been in progress locally for some time over the ownership

长沙路149弄2号信义公煤号炸弹爆炸案。

1936年1月6日下午2时5分，长沙路149弄20号一处中式住宅的前门内发生炸弹爆炸。该房屋位于长沙路与温州路之间的一条弄堂内，部分被信义公煤号用作办公室。其余部分由该公司一名名为罗德佑（Loo Teh-yeu，羅德佑）的股东居住。

通过一扇未上锁的弹簧门可进入房屋的外院。进一步进入则被一道锁着的铁栅栏门阻挡。炸弹属于铁皮罐类型，是用一只木桶运至现场的。炸弹爆炸将木桶炸得粉碎，分隔内外院的隔断上的多扇窗户被震碎。隔断也受到轻微损坏。无人受伤。在现场发现的木桶碎片显示，它曾被用来盛放油漆或灰泥；还发现了画家所用刷子的小碎片。桶内也曾装有一封信。这封信虽因爆炸受损，但仍可辨认，声称发自“铁血团上海分团”，并包含对汉奸采取进一步行动的威胁。（附译文）。

据该煤号一名名为史济华（Sz Tsih-hwa）的学徒称，一名身穿蓝色衣服（长衫样式）、身高约5英尺5英寸、中等身材的男子放置了炸弹，但未看清其面部。

Extract from Intelligence Report dated January 7, 1936

Bomb explosion at the Sing Nyi Kung Coal Company

At 2.05 p.m. January 6, an unidentified male Chinese deposited a wooden bucket contain_ng a bomb of the canister type inside the main entrance of the Sing Nyi Kung Coal Company (信義公), No.20, Lane 149, Changsha Road. An explosion ensued and a number of windows of the premises were shattered. Among the debris was found a letter in Chinese purporting to emanate from the "Shanghai Branch of the Blood & Soul Group" and addressed to two shareholders of the coal company. The letter accuses the addressees of conspiring with traitors and threatens further action should the warning be ignored.

This act of intimidation is believed to be the outcome of a dispute over the sale locally of coal mined in the province of Hopei.

1月6日下午2时05分，一名身份不明的中国男子将一个装有罐式炸弹的木桶放置在长沙路149弄20号信义公煤号（信義公）的大门口内。随后发生爆炸，该处多扇窗户被震碎。在废墟中发现一封中文信件，声称出自“血魂团上海分团”，寄给该煤号的两位股东。信中指控收信人勾结汉奸，并威胁若无视警告将采取进一步行动。

此次恐吓行为被认为是因河北产煤炭在当地销售引发的纠纷所致。

BOMB EXPLOSION.
At 2.05 p.m. 6-1-36 a telephone message was received from C.C.K. to the effect that a bomb had been thrown into premises occupied by the Sing Nyi Koeng Coal Co., House No.20, Lane 149 Changsha Road.
Police immediately proceeded to the scene, and ascertained the following:- The premises are situated in Lane No.149 a distance of about 50 yards from Changsha Road. A wooden partition has been erected across the court-yard about ten feet inside the front door. An iron grill forms part of this partition, and is always kept locked.
At 2 p.m. six of the inmates were in a down stairs room when the bell on the front door was rung. An apprentice named Su Kyui Yu left the room and proceeded to the iron grill, saw a male Chinese disappearing through the front door-way. The apprentice returned to the room and about one minute later a loud explosion was heard.
Fragments of a bomb were picked up which appeared to be of the ordinary tin cannister type filled with gun powder. Fragments of a small wooden basket were also found where the explosion took place. The bomb had evidently been carried in the basket and placed against the partition in the yard after having lit a short length of fuse attached to the bomb; the culprit made a hurried exit by the front door. No persons injured. A number of panes of glass broken and part of the partition shattered.
A/S.D.I. Webb, Special Branch, attended the scene and found a letter in a torn condition near to where the explosion took place. This letter purporting to have been written by the Shanghai Branch of the Kuomintang and Anti-Japanese Association informing the inmates that the premises were to be bombed. Letter of Punishment from the Shanghai Branch of
the Blood & Soul Corps.

We have received repeated reports from our section stating
that you have been conspiring with the traitors in order to
satisfy your personal desires and endanger public welfare.
Our investigators have confirmed these reports. Besides,
newspapers have also disclosed your secrets. All these
evidences confirm your intrigue which is inexcusable. Although
we intended to kill you at once, we have decided to send an
officer to give a warning first by means of a small bomb. If
you repent your doing and correct your behaviour, our corps
will pardon your life. If you take no notice of our warning
and persist in your actions, we will not notify you again but
put you to death at once. This is to notify you,

Leo Teh Yeu

At 2.05 p.m. January 6, an explosion occurred
in the Sing Nyi Coal Co., Lane 149, House 20, Changsha
Road, causing slight damage. The address in question
is a dwelling-house which is used by a few coal merchants
for trading purposes. It is situated about midway
between Changsha Road and Park Road. The explosion was
caused by a bomb of the canaster type which broke several
windows and did some slight damage to woodwork.

Between December 18 and December 31, five copies
of newspapers containing articles alleging that the
Sing Nyi Co. was dealing in "Hopei" coal were received
at the above address. "Hopei" coal is produced by the
Liu Kiang Coal Mining Co. whose mines were recently
taken over by the Japanese without, it is alleged, the
rightful owners being in any way compensated.

The S.P.O. and C.D.I. Grubb of the Special Branch
are now on the scene making investigations in co-operation
with Station detectives.

Special Branch,
January 6, 1936.

At 2.05 p.m. January 6, an explosion occurred
in the Sing Nyi Coal Co., Lane 149, House 20, Changsha
Road, causing slight damage. The address in question
is a dwelling-house which is used by a few coal merchants
for trading purposes. It is situated about midway
between Changsha Road and Park Road. The explosion was
caused by a bomb of the canaster type which broke several
windows and did some slight damage to woodwork.

Between December 18 and December 31, five copies
of newspapers containing articles alleging that the
Sing Nyi Co. was dealing in "Hopei" coal were received
at the above address. "Hopei" coal is produced by the
Liu Kiang Coal Mining Co. whose mines were recently
taken over by the Japanese without, it is alleged, the
rightful owners being in any way compensated.

The S.P.O. and C.D.I. Grubb of the Special Branch
are now on the scene making investigations in co-operation
with Station detectives.

Subject Summary of the agitation in the local coal market.
Made by D. P. S. Mackey Forwarded by [签名]
Following the extension of Japanese interests in
North China, the mines of the Liu Kiang (柳江) Coal Mining
Company, 480 Nanking Road, in Linyu Hsien (临榆县), Hopei,
were seized by a Japanese firm, the Tai Kee (泰記) Mining
Company. This concern continued to operate the mines and
shipped their products to Shanghai under the name of "Hopei"
coal, appointing a local Chinese named Ma Sao-chien (馬少荃)
as their Shanghai agent. Ma formed the Chung Fu (中孚)
Mining Company, Room 512, 470 Hankow Road, and announced his
agency in the Chinese press.
Meanwhile the Liu Kiang Company had made public the
facts of the seizure of their mines, and as a result the
Shanghai Municipality Coal Merchants' Association expelled
from membership three coal companies who were dealing in coal
from the seized mines. The Bureau of Social Affairs took up
this matter on behalf of the expelled companies, and informed
the Shanghai Municipality Coal Merchants' Association that
their decision should be withdrawn and that in future no
member should be expelled from the Association without the
prior approval of the Bureau. Dissatisfied at this inter-
ference, the Shanghai Municipality Coal Merchants' Association
appealed to the local Tangpu for a ruling in the matter. The
Tangpu decreed that the Association should warn all its
members not to deal in "Hopei" coal, but to date has taken
no action in the matter of the expulsion of the three companies.
The Shanghai Municipality Coal Merchants' Association then
petitioned the Bureau of Social Affairs for the withdrawal of
the order regarding the expulsion of the companies, and at
the same time decided to acquaint the public with the facts.

Subject Local Tangpu and the Chung Fu Mine Company.
Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

In accordance with instructions, I interviewed
Mr. Wang Ma, the Chief of the 3rd Department, and Lu Yuen Fu
of the local Tangpu and called their attention to the activities
of certain coal merchants in Shanghai which are liable to
bring about an anti-Japanese boycott.
Mr. Lu expresses the opinion that a majority of the
Tangpu members are opposed to the newly formed Chung Fu Coal
Company especially as it is under one Ma Siao Chuen, a follower
of Wong Yien Sung(王延松). Besides being connected with
the Standing Committee of the local Tangpu Mr. Wong is a
member of the Chamber of Commerce, a member of the Advisory
Committee of the S.M.C., the proprietor of the Hwa Hwa Silk
Store, Nanking Road, and the Silk Merchants Bank on Hankow
Road. He made his money through the boycott movements some
years ago.
It appears that the Liu Kiang Coal Company at Ling Yu
Hsien, East Hopei, had secured a monopoly from the Nanking
Government and the Provincial Government of Hopei for working
the mines located in the Hsien but the monopoly became value-
less after the forcible occupation of the mines by the Japanese
which was followed by the formation of the Tai Kee Mining

Sung Chien Ng (孫 廉 午 ) of the Tai Kee Company petitioned for an enlargement of the company's mining district. The magistrate of that district discovered that Sung Chien Ng had attempted to encroach upon the land belonging to Chang Tuh Hsiung and the Liukiang Coal Company. Upon protests lodged by the latter, the Tai Kee Company gave up their attempt. In July of the 9th year of the Chinese Republic, the former Industrial Department of Chihli Province instructed the magistrate to ascertain whether or not there had been any disputes between the Liukiang Coal Company and neighbouring mines. The investigation was conducted by Sung Hua Tso (孫 幼 聰) and Wang (王) of the Tai Kee Company, and Kai Kuei Feng (閻 桂 芬) of the Pao Shing Company who proceeded to the Liukiang Coal Company. "(B) On July 22 in the 3rd year of the Chinese Republic, Chang Tuh Hsiung requested permission to make a trial exploitation of the Hai Sai Yao Mining District. The request was granted on September 8, and the license was valid until September 7 of the 8th year of the Chinese Republic. On August 2 in the 8th year of the Chinese Republic, Chang Tuh Hsiung and Li Iau petitioned for permission to exploit the mine in the name of the Liukiang Coal Company, to which a permit to exploit the mine was issued on November 3 in the 9th year of the Chinese Republic.

"In view of the foregoing two points, the Tai Kee Company has no legal basis and is therefore in the wrong."

Responsibilities of the Tai Kee Company from legal point of view.

(A) Notwithstanding the fact that the Tai Kee Company is a Sino-Japanese concern, it is registered with the Chinese Government and should therefore be subject to Chinese law. Clause No.8 of the regulations of the Tai Kee Company stipulates:- 'All procedure and acts of the management of the company shall be carried out in accordance with the laws and measures promulgated by the Republic of China.' It is quite clear that the Tai Kee Company cannot act in violation of the law. The right to exploit the Hai Sai Yao Coal Mine was secured long ago by the Liukiang Coal Company and has been confirmed by the highest authorities in the district. The Tai Kee Company has no right whatever to interfere with it. Even should there be some dispute, it should be settled by due process of law. However, the Liukiang Coal Company has now been sealed up by order of E. Ishida of the Tai Kee Company and its property valued at several million dollars has been illegally encroached upon. The Tai Kee Company should be held responsible for the losses sustained by the Liukiang Coal Company.

(B) Clause No.6 of the agreement of the Tai Kee Company says: 'Sung Chien Ng shall be the representative of the company.' In their requests for permission to exploit the mines, all documents were signed by Sung Chien Ng on behalf of the Tai Kee Company. The Japanese has no right to represent the concern. In the present forcible occupation of the Liukiang Coal Company, the Tai Kee Company placed the sealing order in the name of E. Ishida who acted as the company's representative. If E. Ishida has any claim on the Liukiang Coal Company, he should proceed according to the principles of Consular Jurisdiction and the defendant should be tried by a Chinese tribunal. However, E. Ishida

泰记公司的孙廉午请求扩大公司矿区。该地区知事发现孙廉午企图侵占属于张笃雄和六江煤矿公司的土地。鉴于后者提出抗议，泰记公司放弃了这一企图。民国九年七月，直隶省前实业厅指令知事查明六江煤矿公司与邻近矿井之间是否存在任何纠纷。调查由泰记公司的孙幼聪和王氏，以及宝兴公司的阎桂芬前往六江煤矿公司进行。他们发现根本没有任何纠纷。

“(B) 民国三年七月二十二日，张笃雄请求允许试采海赛窑矿区。该请求于九月八日获准，执照有效期至民国八年九月七日。民国八年八月二日，张笃雄和李耀以六江煤矿公司的名义申请开采该矿，并于民国九年十一月三日颁发开采许可证。

“鉴于上述两点，泰记公司没有法律依据，因此理亏。”

从法律角度看泰记公司的责任。

(A) 尽管泰记公司是一家中日合资企业，但它在中国政府注册，因此应受中国法律管辖。泰记公司章程第八条规定：“公司管理的所有程序和行动应按照中华民国颁布的法律和措施进行。”显然，泰记公司不能违法行事。海赛窑煤矿的开采权早已由六江煤矿公司获得，并得到该地区最高当局的确认。泰记公司无权干涉。即使存在争议，也应通过正当法律程序解决。然而，六江煤矿公司现在被泰记公司的石田E.（E. Ishida）下令查封，其价值数百万美元的财产遭到非法侵占。泰记公司应对六江煤矿公司遭受的损失承担责任。

(B) 泰记公司协议第六条规定：“孙廉午为公司代表。”在申请开采许可时，所有文件均由孙廉午代表泰记公司签署。该日本人无权代表该企业。在目前强行占领六江煤矿公司的事件中，泰记公司以担任公司代表的石田E.的名义张贴封条。如果石田E.对六江煤矿公司有任何权利要求，他应根据领事裁判权原则行事，被告应由中国法庭审判。然而，石田E.

昨日下午4时，上海煤炭同业公会执行委员会和监察委员会成员魏鸿文等人召开联席会议，通过以下决议：
1) 关于六江煤矿公司来信，请求对作为销售“被盗”煤炭代理的信义恒和又新煤炭商行采取制裁措施一事，对上述两家商行的处理方式应与东大成商行的处理方式相同。

Shanghai Public Daily News published the following editorial on
December 19, 1935:-

SANCTIONS AGAINST TREACHEROUS MERCHANTS.

Our hatred of treacherous merchants is several times
greater than our hatred of our "friendly nation" which has invaded
our country with rifles and guns. We are not surprised that we
are being oppressed by foreign nations, but the treacherous
merchants are of the same race as we are and yet they are heart-
less and prefer to act as the running-dogs of imperialists for a
small profit. In their avarice, they have forsaken the interests
of their country.

Fundamentally, treacherous merchants and the country
cannot exist at the same time, therefore we should apply sanctions
against the treacherous merchants. We cannot do this work by mere
talk because treacherous merchants have money and persons who talk
of applying sanctions against treacherous merchants can be induced
to compromise. It may be recalled that during the May 30 Incident,
an Anti-Japanese Association worked energetically against
treacherous merchants. The result is an open secret. The goods
belonging to treacherous merchants went into the hands of the leaders
of the movement to apply sanctions against treacherous merchants.
(Of course there were exceptions). It was reported that at the
dissolution of the Anti-Japanese Association there was left behind
a large amount of national salvation fund which included a sum of
$100,000 appropriated for the establishment of a labour school.
Where is this school? Where is the money? It is still a mystery.

While the national crisis is growing acute, a number
of treacherous merchants have sprung up out of the movement to apply
sanctions against treacherous merchants. We must conduct this
movement honestly in order to safeguard our national interests.
In this way only can we apply sanctions against treacherous merchants.

We must unite and endeavour to resist foreign
aggression. We must apply sanctions against the treacherous
merchants who care for money only, to the utter disregard of the

《上海市民日报》于1935年12月19日发表以下社论：

制裁奸商。

我们对奸商的仇恨比对我们那个用步枪和大炮入侵我国的“友邦”的仇恨要大好几倍。我们对外国列强的压迫并不感到惊讶，但奸商与我们同属一个种族，却无情地为了微利甘愿充当帝国主义的走狗。出于贪婪，他们抛弃了国家利益。

从根本上说，奸商与国家不能共存，因此我们应该对奸商实施制裁。我们不能仅靠空谈来做这项工作，因为奸商有钱，而那些谈论对奸商实施制裁的人可能会被诱导妥协。回想一下，在五卅运动期间，一个反日协会积极致力于打击奸商。结果是一个公开的秘密。属于奸商的货物落入了领导打击奸商运动的领导人手中。（当然也有例外）。据报道，在反日协会解散时，留下了一大笔救国基金，其中包括拨用于建立一所劳工学校的10万元。这所学校在哪里？钱在哪里？这仍然是一个谜。

随着民族危机日益加剧，一些奸商从打击奸商运动中涌现出来。我们必须诚实地开展这场运动，以维护我们的国家利益。只有这样，我们才能对奸商实施制裁。

我们必须团结起来，努力抵抗外国侵略。我们必须对那些只关心金钱、完全无视

December 20, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers :-

LIUKIANG COAL MINE COMPANY SUBMITS APPEAL TO THE LOCAL TANGPU
(continued from yesterday)

Acting on the request of the Liukiang Coal Mine Company, the local General Labour Union at once submitted petitions to the Ministry of Industry and the local Tangpu, requesting them to conduct immediately enquiries and to adopt strict measures to deal with Ma Soo Chien (马少千), the manager of the Chung Fu Company (中孚公司). Yesterday (December 18) the local Coal Trade Association again sent delegates to petition the local Tangpu and other political organs for assistance.

The following joint petition was sent yesterday to the Shanghai General Citizens Federation by the various branches of the Shanghai First Special District Citizens Federation:-

"We became greatly enraged when we noticed in local newspapers about the petition of the local General Labour Union, requesting the Ministry of Industry and the local Tangpu to deal severely with the traitor Ma Soo Chien, the manager of the Chung Fu Company. The illegal occupation of the coal mines of the Liukiang Company at Ling Yu Hsien (灵榆县), Hopei Province, by the Tai Kee Company (泰记公司) is not only a direct blow to the Liukiang Coal Mine Company but also causes a serious loss to our national finances. Such a state of affairs is certainly very much to be regretted by the entire Chinese nation.

"However, Ma Soo Chien, a committee member of the local Chinese Chamber of Commerce, being a business leader of the local Chinese community, has established the so-called Chung Fu Company on the premises of the Shanghai Silk Industry, Commerical and Savings Bank, and has openly and very shamelessly announced in the newspapers that this company would act as an agent for the disposal of the "stolen" coal. In view of this fact, we submit this joint petition with a request that your Federation will enforce some strict sanctions against the Chung Fu Company."

（批：SI, Please attach this to your next report on coal situation and comment on contents. What is the exact title of the General Citizens' Federation? Where did they hold the meeting? Is your Chinese staff watching this movement? JWS）

Upon receipt of the above petition, the Special District Citizens Federation have called a meeting of its Standing Committee members and have passed the following resolutions:-
(1) That the Chamber of Commerce be requested to dispense with the services of Ma Soo Chien.
(2) That the Wusih Fellow-Countrymen Association be requested to expel Ma Soo Chien.
(3) That the public be notified of the actions of Ma Soo Chien.
(4) That the Coal Mine Trade Association be asked to publish immediately all the illegal activities of Ma Soo Chien.

（批：1st）

六河沟煤矿公司呈请当地党部
（续昨日）

应六河沟煤矿公司之请求，当地总工会立即向实业部及当地党部递交请愿书，要求立即进行调查，并对中孚公司经理马少千采取严厉措施。昨日（12月18日），当地煤炭同业公会再次派遣代表向当地党部及其他政治机关请愿求助。

上海第一特区市民联合会各分会昨日向上海市民联合会总会上呈了如下联合请愿书：-

“我们在本地报纸上看到当地总工会呈请实业部及当地党部严惩中孚公司经理、汉奸马少千的请愿书后，感到无比愤慨。泰记公司在河北省灵榆县非法占领六河沟公司的煤矿，这不仅是对六河沟煤矿公司的直接打击，也造成我国财政的严重损失。此种事态诚令全中国人民深感痛惜。

“然而，马少千身为当地华人商会委员，作为当地华人社区的商界领袖，竟在上海丝业商业银行旧址设立所谓的中孚公司，并在报纸上公然无耻地宣布该公司将代理处置‘盗采’煤炭。鉴于此事实，我们呈递此联合请愿书，恳请贵会对中孚公司实施严厉制裁。”

（批注：SI，请将此附在你下一份关于煤炭局势的报告后，并对内容加以评论。市民联合会的确切名称是什么？他们在哪里举行的会议？你的华人员工是否在关注这一动向？JWS）

收到上述请愿书后，特区市民联合会召开了常务委员会会议，并通过了以下决议：-
(1) 请求商会解除马少千的职务。
(2) 请求无锡同乡会开除马少千。
(3) 向公众通报马少千的行为。
(4) 要求煤炭同业公会立即公布马少千的所有非法活动。

（批注：1st）

LIUKIANG COAL MINE COMPANY SUBMITS APPEAL TO THE LOCAL
TANGKU

Owing to the fact that its coal mines at Hai
Sai Yao (黑山窯) in Ling Yu Hsien (臨榆縣), Hopei
Province, have been taken over by the Tai Lee Company
(泰記公司), a Sino-Japanese concern, which is illegally
transporting its coal by Japanese steamers to Shanghai
for sale through the Chung Fu Company (中孚公司),
established by Ma Shao Tsai (馬少), the Liukiang Coal
Mine Company, a Chinese enterprise, which has suffered
much loss, yesterday made an appeal to the local Tangku
for assistance.

The following is an abridged translation of the
appeal:-

"This company has been mining coal in Ling Yu
Hsien, Hopei Province, for about 20 years. Unexpectedly,
in March this year (1935), the Tai Lee Company, a Sino-
Japanese concern, taking advantage of the trouble in North
China and under the protection of the Japanese influence,
illegally occupied and seized our properties in the coal
mining area as well as our coal station at Chimmwangtso
Station and our stocks of coal. Repeated negotiations have
been opened but have had no result.

"Since its occupation of our coal mines, the
Tai Lee Coy. has illegally started working our coal mines
and has even transported stocks to Shanghai for disposal
through the Chung Fu Company as Hopei anthracite.

"Although the Tai Lee Coy. is a Sino-Japanese
concern, it is registered with the Chinese Government and
has been granted permission to operate in accordance with
the Chinese Law Governing the Operation of Coal Mines."

“自占领我们的煤矿以来，泰记公司非法开始开采我们的煤矿，甚至将库存运至上海，通过中孚公司作为河北无烟煤进行处置。

“虽然泰记公司是中日合资企业，但它已在中国政府注册，并已获准按照《中国煤矿经营法》运营。”

History of the Tai Kee Company

On June 24 of the 3rd Year of the Chinese
Republic, Sung Chien Ng ( 宋建業 ), the statutory agent
of the Tai Kee Company submitted a petition for the
trial operation of the coal mines at Shih Meng Sai
( 石門寨 ). As a result of investigations conducted by
the First District Coal Mines Affairs Inspectorate, it
was found that these coal mines were not located at Shih
Meng Tsai, but within the coal mine districts of Liukiang
Village which were being operated by Li Shih. Consequently,
no permission was granted for the trial operation of the
coal mines. On August 10 of the same year, another
petition was submitted for the trial operation of the coal
mines in a neighbouring district, measuring 5,400 mow.
It was again found that this coal area was located within
the Hai Sai Yao Coal Mines operated by Chang Teh Hsiung.
Later the Tai Kee Company marked on the map the coal
mining area to the east of line No. 2 to line No. 9,
measuring 1,236 mow as being operated by Chang Teh Hsiung,
while the company would operate the remaining area, 4,339
mow. A permit for trial operation of the coal mines was
then issued on August 24 in the same year. On August 17
of the 5th Year of the Chinese Republic, the company
applied for the issue of a formal operation permit. On
February 28 of the 6th Year of the Chinese Republic, a
formal permit, No. 194, Character Tsai ( 採 ), for the
operation of the area, measuring 4,339 mow was issued by
the Ministry of Agriculture and Commerce.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers :-

LIUKIANG COAL MINE COMPANY SUBMITS APPEAL TO THE LOCAL TANGPU

Owing to the fact that its coal mine at the Hai Sai Yao (海塞窯) in Ling Yu Hsien (靈榆縣), Hopei Province is illegally occupied by the Tai Kee Company (泰記公司), a Sino-Japanese concern, the local Liukiang Coal Mine Company (柳江煤礦公司), a Chinese enterprise, who have suffered much loss by this action, yesterday submitted an appeal to the local Tangpu requesting assistance.
The following is an abridged translation of the appeal:-

"This company has been mining coal in Ling Yu Hsien, Hopei Province, for about 20 years. Unexpectedly, in May last, the Tai Kee Company, a Sino-Japanese concern, taking advantage of the North China Imbroglio, illegally occupied and seized all our properties in the coal mining area as well as our coal station at the Chingwantao Railway Station and our stocks, under the protection of the Japanese influence. Although repeated negotiations have been opened, no result has as yet been achieved.

"Since its occupation of our coal mines, the Tai Kee Company has illegally started mining the coal and has even transported our stocks to Shanghai for disposal through the Chung Fu Company (中孚公司), under the name of Hopei anthracite. Although this company is a Sino-Japanese concern, it was registered with the Chinese Government authorities and was granted permission to operate in accordance with the Chinese Law Governing the Operation of Coal Mines. As the statutory agent of this firm is a Chinese as is mentioned in its agreement, it is therefore operated in a similar legal status to our company. Therefore, it has no right to occupy our coal mines. Even if there exist legal disputes between us, they should be subject to the jurisdiction of Chinese Law.

"Although our company has petitioned the Hopei Reconstruction Department to instruct the district authorities to put a stop to such a practice on the part of the Tai Kee Company, the latter firm has, however, ignored such instructions.

"Apart from petitioning the National Government to open negotiations on this matter and requesting the local Chinese Chamber of Commerce and the Coal Trade Association to adopt an impartial attitude to deal with the disposal of the "stolen" coal in Shanghai by the Tai Kee Company, we have to submit you this petition together with the advertisements which we published in the newspapers on October 23 and December 14 respectively, requesting you to render us assistance so as to enable us to preserve our property, the coal mines at Hai Sai Yao, Ling Yu Hsien, Hopei Province."

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：-

柳江煤矿公司向当地党部提出申诉

鉴于河北省灵榆县（Ling Yu Hsien）海塞窑（Hai Sai Yao）的煤矿被中日合资企业泰记公司（Tai Kee Company）非法侵占，遭受巨大损失的中国企业柳江煤矿公司（Liukiang Coal Mine Company）昨日向当地党部提出申诉，请求援助。
以下是申诉书的节译：-

“本公司在河北省灵榆县开采煤矿已有约20年历史。不料去年五月，中日合资企业泰记公司利用华北事变之机，在日本势力的庇护下，非法侵占并夺取了我们在矿区的所有财产，以及在秦皇岛火车站的煤站和库存。虽经多次交涉，迄今未有结果。

“自侵占我方煤矿以来，泰记公司非法开始采煤，甚至通过中孚公司（Chung Fu Company），以河北无烟煤的名义，将我们的库存运往上海处置。虽然该公司是中日合资企业，但它已在中国政府当局注册，并根据中国《矿业法》获得经营许可。由于其协议中规定该公司的法定代理人为中国人，因此其法律地位与我公司类似。因此，它无权侵占我们的煤矿。即使双方存在法律纠纷，也应受中国法律的管辖。

“虽然我公司已请河北省建设厅指令地方当局制止泰记公司的此类行为，但该公司却无视这些指令。

“除了提请国民政府就此事项进行谈判，并请求当地中华总商会和煤炭同业公会对泰记公司在上海处置‘赃’煤采取公正态度外，我们不得不向贵处提交本申诉书，并附上我们分别于10月23日和12月14日在报纸上刊登的广告，请求贵处给予援助，以便我们保全位于河北省灵榆县海塞窑的煤矿财产。”

当地党部收到柳江煤矿公司的申诉后，立即委派官员进行必要调查，证实申诉内容属实。因此，党部发布了以下

THE OPIUM-SUPPRESSION MOVEMENT

The registration of opium smokers
by the Bureau of Public Safety will be completed in
two weeks time. The opium-curing hospitals in active
preparation will be established in the near future.
With a view to eradicating the
opium evil throughout this municipality, the Bureau of
Public Safety is making every effort to arrange with
the Police Departments of the French Concession and the
International Settlement for assistance in the arrest
of all the opium smokers within their jurisdiction. It
is believed that such measures will be enforced soon and
that there will be a hope of stopping all opium smoking

MONEY & PISTOLS FOUND BURIED IN THE MUD.

Shortly after 3 p.m. the other day,
Zee Tsoh Kwei (徐佐貴), Tsiang Kwei Lan (蔣桂蘭),
Kao Lien She (高連喜), Zee Mou Zung (徐某人) and
3 other Kompo coolies were engaged by the Public Works
Bureau to remove mud in the vicinity of Pei Hsin Ching
(北新), Western District. Suddenly, a large
package, wrapped with paper, was discovered lying in
the mud and was then taken out by Zee Tsoh Kwei who
arranged with the three abovementioned persons to meet
later at the Kao Sun (高順) Bath House at Zao Ka Doo
(曹家渡).
When they met, Zee Tsoh Kwei produced
$70 which was to be divided among the three others, but
detectives of the Branch Bureau of Public Safety at
Zao Ka Doo arrived on the spot and arrested three of them.
Zee Tsoh Kwei made good his escape prior to the arrival
of the detectives.
According to the statements taken
from the accused, the package consists of two pistols
of which one is an imitation. They do not know how many
legal tender notes there are in the package.
Zee Tsoh Kwei now at large and is
wanted by the Chinese Police.

禁烟运动

泥中发现金钱与手枪。

日前下午3点后不久，徐佐貴（Zee Tsoh Kwei）、蔣桂蘭（Tsiang Kwei Lan）、高連喜（Kao Lien She）、徐某人（Zee Mou Zung）及其他3名工部局苦力受工务局雇佣，在西区北新泾（Pei Hsin Ching）附近清除淤泥。突然，发现一个大包裹裹着纸躺在泥中，随即被徐佐貴取出，并与上述三人约定稍后在曹家渡（Zao Ka Doo）的高顺（Kao Sun）浴室见面。
见面时，徐佐貴拿出70元打算分给其他三人，但曹家渡公安分局的侦探赶到现场，逮捕了其中三人。徐佐貴在侦探到达前逃脱。
根据被告的供词，包裹内有两把手枪，其中一把是仿制品。他们不知道包裹内有多少法定货币钞票。
徐佐貴目前在逃，正被中国警方通缉。

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers :-

LIUKIANG COAL MINE COMPANY SUBMITS APPEAL TO THE LOCAL TANGPU

Owing to the fact that its coal mine
at the Hai Sai Yao (海賽窯) in Ling Yu Hsien (靈榆縣),
Hopei Province is illegally occupied by the Tai Kee Company
(泰記公司), a Sino-Japanese concern, the local Liukiang
Coal Mine Company (柳江煤礦公司), a Chinese enterprise, who
have suffered much loss by this action, yesterday submitted
an appeal to the local Tangpu requesting assistance.
The following is an abridged translation
of the appeal:-

"This company has been mining coal
in Ling Yu Hsien, Hopei Province, for about 20 years.
Unexpectedly, in May last, the Tai Kee Company, a Sino-
Japanese concern, taking advantage of the North China
Imbroglio, illegally occupied and seized all our properties
in the coal mining area as well as our coal station at the
Chingwantao Railway Station and our stocks, under the
protection of the Japanese influence. Although
repeated negotiations have been opened, no result has as
yet been achieved.

"Since its occupation of our coal
mines, the Tai Kee Company has illegally started
mining the coal and has even transported our stocks to
Shanghai for disposal through the Chung Fu Company (中孚公司),
under the name of Hopei anthracite. Although this company
is a Sino-Japanese concern, it was registered with the
Chinese Government authorities and was granted permission
to operate in accordance with the Chinese Law Governing
the Operation of Coal Mines. As the statutory agent of
this firm is a Chinese as is mentioned in its agreement,
it is therefore operated in a similar legal status to
our company. Therefore, it has no right to occupy our
coal mines. Even if there exist legal disputes between
us, they should be subject to the jurisdiction of Chinese
Law.

"Although our company has petitioned
the Hopei Reconstruction Department to instruct the district
authorities to put a stop to such a practice on the part
of the Tai Kee Company, the latter firm has, however,
ignored such instructions.

"Apart from petitioning the National
Government to open negotiations on this matter and requesting
the local Chinese Chamber of Commerce and the Coal Trade
Association to adopt an impartial attitude to deal with
the disposal of the "stolen" coal in Shanghai by the Tai
Kee Company, we have to submit you this petition together
with the advertisements which we published in newspapers
on October 23 and December 14 respectively, requesting you
to render us assistance so as to enable us to preserve our
property, the coal mines at Hai Sai Yao, Ling Yu Hsien,
Hopei Province."

After receipt of the petition from
the Liukiang Coal Mine Company, the local Tangpu has
immediately delegated officials to conduct necessary
enquiries which elicit that the contents of the petition
are true. The Tangpu, therefore, issued the following

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：-

柳江煤矿公司向当地党部提交请愿书

由于位于河北省灵榆县（Ling Yu Hsien）海赛窑（Hai Sai Yao）的煤矿被中日合资企业泰记公司（Tai Kee Company）非法占领，遭受巨大损失的中国企业柳江煤矿公司（Liukiang Coal Mine Company）于昨日向当地党部提交请愿书，请求援助。
以下是请愿书的摘要译文：-

“本公司在河北省灵榆县开采煤矿已有约20年历史。不料去年5月，中日合资企业泰记公司利用华北事变之机，在日本势力的庇护下，非法占领并查封了我们在矿区的所有财产，以及我们在秦皇岛火车站的煤站和库存。尽管进行了多次谈判，但至今未取得结果。

“自从占领我们的煤矿以来，泰记公司非法开始采煤，甚至通过中孚公司（Chung Fu Company）以河北无烟煤的名义将我们的库存运往上海处置。虽然该公司是中日合资企业，但它已在中国政府机关注册，并根据《中国煤矿经营法》获得运营许可。由于其协议中提到的法定代理人是中国人，因此其法律地位与我公司相似。因此，它无权占领我们的煤矿。即使我们之间存在法律纠纷，也应受中国法律的管辖。

“虽然我公司已 petitioned 河北复兴局指令地方当局制止泰记公司的此类行为，但该公司却无视这些指令。

“除了请愿国民政府就此事项展开谈判，并请求当地中华总商会和煤业同业公会采取公正态度处理泰记公司在上海处置‘被盗’煤炭一事外，我们不得不向您提交此请愿书，并附上我们分别于10月23日和12月14日在报纸上刊登的广告，请求您给予我们援助，以便我们能够保全我们在河北省灵榆县海赛窑的财产——煤矿。”

当地党部收到柳江煤矿公司的请愿书后，立即委派官员进行必要调查，调查结果证实请愿书内容属实。因此，党部发布了以下

SEVERE PUNISHMENT SHOULD BE IMPOSED ON TREACHEROUS MERCHANTS WHO SELL "STOLEN" COAL

During this period of turmoil the number of traitors and treacherous merchants is increasing. While the nation is on the verge of ruin these merchants are anxious about their personal interests only and have no regard for the welfare of the people. In order to save the nation from ruin these merchants should be eliminated.

When an anti-Japanese Association was in existence in this city, treacherous merchants were a little afraid, but today, owing to the government having warned the people not to carry out any anti-Japanese movement, these merchants are beginning to be active again. We were surprised to find that the leading agitators in a former anti-Japanese movement had amassed great wealth and have become traitors also. Therefore, when one finds that one can become rich through an anti-Japanese movement one can become richer still by conspiring with Japan.

Recently the Chung Fu Co. entered into an agreement with the Tung Dah Cheng and Tuen Yeh Cheng coal hangs for the sale of "stolen" coal from the Liukiang Coal Mining Co. This agreement has aroused strong opposition from the public. The Liukiang Coal Mining Co. is a member of the Coal Merchants' Association and has been licensed to mine coal in Lin Yuan Hsien, Hopei, for the last 20 years. It has a capital of three million dollars subscribed entirely by Chinese and it has nothing to do with the neighboring colliery, the Tai Koo Co., operated by Chinese and Japanese. —《市民日报》（Shanghai Daily News）于1935年12月18日发表如下社论：

严惩贩卖“盗采”煤炭的奸商

在此动荡时期，汉奸与奸商的数量日益增加。当国家濒临灭亡之际，这些商人只顾个人利益，毫不顾及民众福祉。为了挽救国家免于灭亡，必须清除这些商人。

本市存在抗日协会时，奸商们尚存几分畏惧，但如今，由于政府警告民众不得进行任何抗日运动，这些商人又开始活跃起来。我们惊讶地发现，前次抗日运动中的主要煽动者已积聚巨额财富，并也变成了汉奸。因此，人们发现通过抗日运动可以致富，而通过与日本勾结则可以更加富有。

近期，中福公司（Chung Fu Co.）与同大成（Tung Dah Cheng）及元业成（Tuen Yeh Cheng）煤号达成协议，销售来自六河沟煤矿公司（Liukiang Coal Mining Co.）的“盗采”煤炭。此协议引起了公众的强烈反对。六河沟煤矿公司是煤炭同业公会会员，过去20年来一直获准在河北临城县开采煤炭。其资本为三百万元，全部由华人认购，与邻近由中日合办的太古公司（Tai Koo Co.）经营的煤矿无关。1935年3月5日，正值华北因中日问题处于危急时刻，太古公司派遣一名名为石田（Ishida）的日本人及数名日本警察，在六河沟煤矿公司拥有的矿区内设立界碑。5月4日，他们强占了六河沟煤矿及石家庄车站的煤栈。11月26日，一批重约

Our Chinese colliery was illegally seized by the Tai

December 13, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

NIPPO(12-12-35)

CHINESE COAL MERCHANTS OBSTRUCT JAPANESE COAL BUSINESS.

Recently the Tai Kee Coal
Mining Company(Japanese) bought up the Liukiang Coal
Mining Company which had a coal mine at Shihmen, Hopei near to
its own coal mine and has now established a Sino-Japanese
Coal Mining Company to manage the two coal mines together.
The distribution of the Liukiang
coal in Shanghai was being undertaken by the Tsung Fu
Company besides a certain Japanese firm.
On December 10 the Shanghai
Chinese Coal Merchants Guild called an urgent meeting which
was attended by 200 members and unanimously passed a
resolution to the effect that two member merchants Messrs
Teng Dah Cheng and Messrs Hsu Nyi Yung be expelled from
the coal market on the grounds that they are dealing with
Japanese coal having concluded contracts with the Tsung
Fu Company. This action clearly obstructs the Japanese
coal business. For this reason the Japanese coal merchants
have become highly indignant and hope that the Chinese
will reconsider the matter as quickly as possible.

NIPPO（1935年12月12日）

中国煤商阻碍日本煤炭业务。

近期，太记煤矿公司（日资）收购了在河北石门拥有煤矿、且毗邻其自身煤矿的六河沟煤矿公司，并现已成立一家中日煤矿公司，共同管理这两处煤矿。
六河沟煤炭在上海的分销工作，除某家日本商社外，一直由中福公司（Tsung Fu Company）承担。
12月10日，上海华商煤炭同业公会召开紧急会议，200名会员出席，并一致通过决议，以滕大成先生（Messrs Teng Dah Cheng）和徐义荣先生（Messrs Hsu Nyi Yung）两名会员商人与中福公司签订合同、经营日本煤炭为由，将其驱逐出煤炭市场。此举显然阻碍了日本煤炭业务。鉴于此，日本煤商极为愤慨，希望中方尽快重新考虑此事。
